[136](https://docs.rs#136)//! # Without macros
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//! `manyhow` can be used without proc macros, and they can be disabled by
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//! adding `manyhow` with `default-features=false`.
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//!
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//! The usage is more or less the same, though with some added boilerplate from
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//! needing to invoke one of [`function()`] ([`function!`]), [`attribute()`]
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//! ([`attribute!`]) or [`derive()`] ([`derive!`]) directly. For each version
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//! there exists a function and a `macro_rules` macro, while the function only
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//! supports [`proc_macro::TokenStream`] and [`proc_macro2::TokenStream`], the
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//! macro versions also support any type that implements [`Parse`]
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//! and [`ToTokens`] respectively.
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//!
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//! While the examples use closures, functions can be passed in as well. The
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//! above example would then change to:
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//! ```
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//! # use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//! # use quote::quote;
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! # use syn2 as syn;
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//! use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//!
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//! # let _ = quote!{
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//! #[proc_macro]
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//! # };
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//! pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! # let tmp = input.clone();
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//! # let output: TokenStream =
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//!     manyhow::function(
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//!         input,
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!         false,
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//!         |input: TokenStream2| -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//!             // ..
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//! #           Ok(quote!())
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//!         },
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!     )
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//! # ;
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//! # let input = tmp;
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//!     // Or
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//!     manyhow::function!(
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//!         input,
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//!         |input: syn::DeriveInput| -> manyhow::Result<syn::ItemImpl> {
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//!             // ..
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! #           manyhow::bail!("error")
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//!         },
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//!     )
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//! }
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! ```
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//! [`Emitter`](#emitter-mut-emitter) and [dummy
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//! `TokenStream`](#dummy-mut-tokenstream) can also be used. [`function()`]
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//! ([`function!`]) and [`attribute()`] ([`attribute!`]) take an additional
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//! boolean parameter controlling whether the input/item will be used as initial
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//! dummy.
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//!
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//! # `emitter: &mut Emitter`
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//! [`*MacroHandler`](FunctionMacroHandler)s (the traits defining what
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//! closures/functions can be used with `manyhow`) can take a mutable reference
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//! to an [`Emitter`]. This allows collecting errors, but not fail immediately.
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//!
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//! [`Emitter::into_result`] can be used to return if an [`Emitter`] contains
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//! any values.
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//!
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//! ```
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//! # use quote::quote;
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//! # use syn2 as syn;
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//! use manyhow::{manyhow, Emitter, ErrorMessage};
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//! use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//!
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//! # let _ = quote!{
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//! #[manyhow]
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//! #[proc_macro]
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//! # };
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//! fn my_macro(input: TokenStream2, emitter: &mut Emitter) -> manyhow::Result<TokenStream2> {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)//!     // ..
[208](https://docs.rs#208)//!     emitter.emit(ErrorMessage::call_site("A fun error!"));
[209](https://docs.rs#209)//!     emitter.into_result()?;
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//!     // ..
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//! #   Ok(quote!())
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//! }
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//! ```
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//!
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//! # `dummy: &mut TokenStream`
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//! [`*MacroHandler`](FunctionMacroHandler)s can also take a mutable reference
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//! to a `TokenStream`, to enable emitting some dummy code to be used in case
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//! the macro errors.
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//!
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//! This allows either appending tokens e.g., with [`ToTokens::to_tokens`] or
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//! directly setting the dummy code e.g., `*dummy = quote!{some tokens}`.
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//!
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//! # Crate features
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//!
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//! - `macros` **default** Enables [`#[manyhow]`](macros::manyhow) attribute
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//!   macro.
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//! - `syn`/`syn2` **default** Enables errors for [`syn` 2.x](https://docs.rs/syn/latest/syn/).
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//! - `syn1` Enables errors for [`syn` 1.x](https://docs.rs/syn/1.0.109/syn/index.html).
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//! - `darling` Enables errors for [`darling`](https://docs.rs/darling/latest/index.html).
[230](https://docs.rs#230)
[231](https://docs.rs#231)#[cfg(feature = "macros")]
[232](https://docs.rs#232)pub use macros::manyhow;
[233](https://docs.rs#233)use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[234](https://docs.rs#234)#[cfg(doc)]
[235](https://docs.rs#235)use {quote::ToTokens, syn2::parse::Parse};
[236](https://docs.rs#236)
[237](https://docs.rs#237)extern crate proc_macro;
[238](https://docs.rs#238)
[239](https://docs.rs#239)#[macro_use]
[240](https://docs.rs#240)mod span_ranged;
[241](https://docs.rs#241)pub use span_ranged::{to_tokens_span_range, SpanRanged};
[242](https://docs.rs#242)#[macro_use]
[243](https://docs.rs#243)mod macro_rules;
[244](https://docs.rs#244)mod error;
[245](https://docs.rs#245)pub use error::*;
[246](https://docs.rs#246)
[247](https://docs.rs#247)mod parse_to_tokens;
[248](https://docs.rs#248)
[249](https://docs.rs#249)#[doc(hidden)]
[250](https://docs.rs#250)pub mod __private {
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    pub use std::prelude::rust_2021::*;
[252](https://docs.rs#252)
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    pub use quote;
[255](https://docs.rs#255)
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    pub use crate::span_ranged::*;
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    pub type Dummy = Option<TokenStream>;
[258](https://docs.rs#258)
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    pub use crate::parse_to_tokens::*;
[260](https://docs.rs#260)}
[261](https://docs.rs#261)
[262](https://docs.rs#262)/// Marker trait for [`proc_macro::TokenStream`] and
[263](https://docs.rs#263)/// [`proc_macro2::TokenStream`]
[264](https://docs.rs#264)pub trait AnyTokenStream: Clone + From<TokenStream> + Into<TokenStream> + Default {}
[265](https://docs.rs#265)impl AnyTokenStream for TokenStream {}
[266](https://docs.rs#266)impl AnyTokenStream for proc_macro::TokenStream {}
[267](https://docs.rs#267)
[268](https://docs.rs#268)#[macro_export]
[269](https://docs.rs#269)#[doc(hidden)]
[270](https://docs.rs#270)macro_rules! __macro_handler {
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    ($name:ident; $($(#attr=$attr:tt)? $n:ident: $input:expr),+; $impl:expr$(; dummy:$dummy:expr)?) => {
[272](https://docs.rs#272)        $crate::__macro_handler! {! $name; $($(#attr=$attr)? $n: $input.clone()),+; $impl $(; $crate::__private::Some($dummy))?}
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    };
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    ($name:ident; $($(#attr=$attr:tt)? $n:ident: $input:expr),+; $impl:expr; dummy) => {
[275](https://docs.rs#275)        $crate::__macro_handler! {! $name; $($(#attr=$attr)? $n: $input),+; $impl; $crate::__private::Dummy::None}
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    };
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    (! $name:ident; $($(#attr=$attr:tt)? $n:ident: $input:expr),+; $impl:expr $(; $dummy:expr)?) => {{
[278](https://docs.rs#278)        use $crate::__private::{ManyhowParse, ManyhowToTokens, ManyhowTry};
[279](https://docs.rs#279)        let implementation = $impl;
[280](https://docs.rs#280)        $(let $n = &$crate::__private::WhatType::new();)+
[281](https://docs.rs#281)        if false {
[282](https://docs.rs#282)            _ = $crate::__private::$name($($n.identify(),)+ $($dummy,)? implementation);
[283](https://docs.rs#283)            unreachable!();
[284](https://docs.rs#284)        } else {
[285](https://docs.rs#285)            match $crate::__private::$name($(
[286](https://docs.rs#286)                {#[allow(unused)]
[287](https://docs.rs#287)                let attr = false;
[288](https://docs.rs#288)                $(let attr = $attr;)?
[289](https://docs.rs#289)                $n.manyhow_parse($input, attr)},
[290](https://docs.rs#290)            )+ $($dummy,)? implementation)
[291](https://docs.rs#291)            {
[292](https://docs.rs#292)                Err(tokens) => tokens.into(),
[293](https://docs.rs#293)                Ok((output, mut tokens, mut dummy)) => {
[294](https://docs.rs#294)                    match (&$crate::__private::WhatType::from(&output)).manyhow_try(output) {
[295](https://docs.rs#295)                        Err(error) => {
[296](https://docs.rs#296)                            dummy.extend(tokens);
[297](https://docs.rs#297)                            tokens = dummy;
[298](https://docs.rs#298)                            (&$crate::__private::WhatType::from(&error)).manyhow_to_tokens(error, &mut tokens);
[299](https://docs.rs#299)                        },
[300](https://docs.rs#300)                        Ok(output) => (&$crate::__private::WhatType::from(&output)).manyhow_to_tokens(output, &mut tokens),
[301](https://docs.rs#301)                    };
[302](https://docs.rs#302)                    tokens.into()
[303](https://docs.rs#303)                }
[304](https://docs.rs#304)            }
[305](https://docs.rs#305)        }
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    }};
[307](https://docs.rs#307)}
[308](https://docs.rs#308)
[309](https://docs.rs#309)/// Handles [`proc_macro_attribute`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/procedural-macros.html#attribute-macros)
[310](https://docs.rs#310)/// implementation
[311](https://docs.rs#311)///
[312](https://docs.rs#312)/// Takes any `TokenStream` for `input` and `item` and returns any
[313](https://docs.rs#313)/// `TokenStream`. If `item_as_dummy = true` the item input will be used as
[314](https://docs.rs#314)/// default dummy code on error. `body` takes a [`AttributeMacroHandler`] with
[315](https://docs.rs#315)/// two `TokenStream` parameters. And an optional [`&mut Emitter`](Emitter) and
[316](https://docs.rs#316)/// a `&mut TokenStream` for storing a dummy output.
[317](https://docs.rs#317)///
[318](https://docs.rs#318)/// ```
[319](https://docs.rs#319)/// # use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
[320](https://docs.rs#320)/// # use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// use manyhow::{attribute, Emitter, Result};
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[323](https://docs.rs#323)/// # let input = quote!();
[324](https://docs.rs#324)/// # let item = quote!();
[325](https://docs.rs#325)/// # let output: TokenStream =
[326](https://docs.rs#326)/// attribute(
[327](https://docs.rs#327)///     input,
[328](https://docs.rs#328)///     item,
[329](https://docs.rs#329)///     false,
[330](https://docs.rs#330)///     |input: TokenStream,
[331](https://docs.rs#331)///      item: TokenStream,
[332](https://docs.rs#332)///      dummy: &mut TokenStream,
[333](https://docs.rs#333)///      emitter: &mut Emitter|
[334](https://docs.rs#334)///      -> Result {
[335](https://docs.rs#335)///         // ..
[336](https://docs.rs#336)///         # Ok(quote!())
[337](https://docs.rs#337)///     },
[338](https://docs.rs#338)/// );
[339](https://docs.rs#339)/// ```
[340](https://docs.rs#340)///
[341](https://docs.rs#341)/// *Note:* When `item_as_dummy = true` the `dummy: &mut TokenStream` will be
[342](https://docs.rs#342)/// initialized with `item`. To override assign a new `TokenStream`:
[343](https://docs.rs#343)/// ```
[344](https://docs.rs#344)/// # use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
[345](https://docs.rs#345)/// use manyhow::{attribute, Result, SilentError};
[346](https://docs.rs#346)/// use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[347](https://docs.rs#347)/// use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
[348](https://docs.rs#348)/// # let input = quote!(input);
[349](https://docs.rs#349)/// let item = quote!(
[350](https://docs.rs#350)///     struct Struct;
[351](https://docs.rs#351)/// );
[352](https://docs.rs#352)/// let output: TokenStream = attribute(
[353](https://docs.rs#353)///     input,
[354](https://docs.rs#354)///     item,
[355](https://docs.rs#355)///     true,
[356](https://docs.rs#356)///     |input: TokenStream,
[357](https://docs.rs#357)///      item: TokenStream,
[358](https://docs.rs#358)///      dummy: &mut TokenStream|
[359](https://docs.rs#359)///      -> Result<TokenStream, SilentError> {
[360](https://docs.rs#360)///         assert_tokens!(dummy.to_token_stream(), {
[361](https://docs.rs#361)///             struct Struct;
[362](https://docs.rs#362)///         });
[363](https://docs.rs#363)///         *dummy = quote! {
[364](https://docs.rs#364)///             struct Struct(HelloWorld);
[365](https://docs.rs#365)///         };
[366](https://docs.rs#366)///         // ..
[367](https://docs.rs#367)///         Err(SilentError)
[368](https://docs.rs#368)///     },
[369](https://docs.rs#369)/// );
[370](https://docs.rs#370)///
[371](https://docs.rs#371)/// assert_tokens! {output, {struct Struct(HelloWorld);}};
[372](https://docs.rs#372)/// ```
[373](https://docs.rs#373)pub fn attribute<
[374](https://docs.rs#374)    Input: AnyTokenStream,
[375](https://docs.rs#375)    Item: AnyTokenStream,
[376](https://docs.rs#376)    Dummy: AnyTokenStream,
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    Output: MacroOutput,
[378](https://docs.rs#378)    Return: AnyTokenStream,
[379](https://docs.rs#379)    Function,
[380](https://docs.rs#380)>(
[381](https://docs.rs#381)    input: impl AnyTokenStream,
[382](https://docs.rs#382)    item: impl AnyTokenStream,
[383](https://docs.rs#383)    item_as_dummy: bool,
[384](https://docs.rs#384)    body: impl AttributeMacroHandler<
[385](https://docs.rs#385)        Function,
[386](https://docs.rs#386)        Item = Item,
[387](https://docs.rs#387)        Input = Input,
[388](https://docs.rs#388)        Dummy = Dummy,
[389](https://docs.rs#389)        Output = Output,
[390](https://docs.rs#390)    >,
[391](https://docs.rs#391)) -> Return {
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    #[allow(unused_mut)]
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    let mut tokens = Dummy::default();
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    let mut tokens = if item_as_dummy {
[395](https://docs.rs#395)        item.clone().into().into()
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    } else {
[397](https://docs.rs#397)        tokens
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    };
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    let mut emitter = Emitter::new();
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    let output = body.call(
[401](https://docs.rs#401)        input.into().into(),
[402](https://docs.rs#402)        item.into().into(),
[403](https://docs.rs#403)        &mut tokens,
[404](https://docs.rs#404)        &mut emitter,
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    );
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    let mut tokens = tokens.into();
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    let mut tokens = match output.convert() {
[408](https://docs.rs#408)        Ok(tokens) => tokens,
[409](https://docs.rs#409)        Err(error) => {
[410](https://docs.rs#410)            error.to_tokens(&mut tokens);
[411](https://docs.rs#411)            tokens
[412](https://docs.rs#412)        }
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    };
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    emitter.to_tokens(&mut tokens);
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    tokens.into()
[416](https://docs.rs#416)}
[417](https://docs.rs#417)
[418](https://docs.rs#418)/// Handles [`proc_macro_attribute`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/procedural-macros.html#attribute-macros)
[419](https://docs.rs#419)/// implementation
[420](https://docs.rs#420)///
[421](https://docs.rs#421)/// Takes any `TokenStream` for `input` and `item` and its return value. If
[422](https://docs.rs#422)/// `#[as_dummy]` is specified on item, it will be used as default
[423](https://docs.rs#423)/// dummy code on error. `body` takes a [`AttributeMacroHandler`] with two
[424](https://docs.rs#424)/// `TokenStream`s or types implementing [`Parse`] parameters and returning a
[425](https://docs.rs#425)/// `TokenStream` or type implementing [`ToTokens`]. And an optional [`&mut
[426](https://docs.rs#426)/// Emitter`](Emitter) and a `&mut TokenStream` for storing a dummy output.
[427](https://docs.rs#427)///
[428](https://docs.rs#428)///
[429](https://docs.rs#429)/// ```
[430](https://docs.rs#430)/// # use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
[431](https://docs.rs#431)/// # use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
[432](https://docs.rs#432)/// use manyhow::{attribute, Emitter, Result};
[433](https://docs.rs#433)/// use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[434](https://docs.rs#434)/// # let input = quote!();
[435](https://docs.rs#435)/// # let item = quote!();
[436](https://docs.rs#436)/// # let output: TokenStream =
[437](https://docs.rs#437)/// attribute!(input, item, |input: TokenStream,
[438](https://docs.rs#438)///                          item: TokenStream,
[439](https://docs.rs#439)///                          dummy: &mut TokenStream,
[440](https://docs.rs#440)///                          emitter: &mut Emitter|
[441](https://docs.rs#441)///  -> Result {
[442](https://docs.rs#442)///     // ..
[443](https://docs.rs#443)///         # Ok(quote!())
[444](https://docs.rs#444)/// });
[445](https://docs.rs#445)/// ```
[446](https://docs.rs#446)///
[447](https://docs.rs#447)/// *Note:* When `#[as_dummy]` is specified the `dummy: &mut TokenStream` will
[448](https://docs.rs#448)/// be initialized with `item`. To override assign a new `TokenStream`:
[449](https://docs.rs#449)/// ```
[450](https://docs.rs#450)/// # use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
[451](https://docs.rs#451)/// # use syn2 as syn;
[452](https://docs.rs#452)/// use manyhow::{attribute, Result, SilentError};
[453](https://docs.rs#453)/// use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[454](https://docs.rs#454)/// use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
[455](https://docs.rs#455)/// # let input = quote!(input);
[456](https://docs.rs#456)/// let item = quote!(
[457](https://docs.rs#457)///     struct Struct;
[458](https://docs.rs#458)/// );
[459](https://docs.rs#459)/// let output: TokenStream = attribute!(
[460](https://docs.rs#460)///     input,
[461](https://docs.rs#461)///     #[as_dummy]
[462](https://docs.rs#462)///     item,
[463](https://docs.rs#463)///     |input: TokenStream,
[464](https://docs.rs#464)///      item: syn::ItemStruct,
[465](https://docs.rs#465)///      dummy: &mut TokenStream|
[466](https://docs.rs#466)///      -> Result<syn::ItemStruct, SilentError> {
[467](https://docs.rs#467)///         assert_tokens!(dummy.to_token_stream(), {
[468](https://docs.rs#468)///             struct Struct;
[469](https://docs.rs#469)///         });
[470](https://docs.rs#470)///         *dummy = quote! {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)///             struct Struct(HelloWorld);
[472](https://docs.rs#472)///         };
[473](https://docs.rs#473)///         // ..
[474](https://docs.rs#474)///         Err(SilentError)
[475](https://docs.rs#475)///     },
[476](https://docs.rs#476)/// );
[477](https://docs.rs#477)///
[478](https://docs.rs#478)/// assert_tokens! {output, {struct Struct(HelloWorld);}};
[479](https://docs.rs#479)/// ```
[480](https://docs.rs#480)#[macro_export]
[481](https://docs.rs#481)macro_rules! attribute {
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    ($input:expr, #[as_dummy] $item:expr, $impl:expr $(,)?) => {
[483](https://docs.rs#483)        $crate::__macro_handler!{attribute_transparent; #attr=true input: $input, item: $item.clone(); $impl; dummy: $item}
[484](https://docs.rs#484)    };
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    ($input:expr, $item:expr, $impl:expr $(,)?) => {
[486](https://docs.rs#486)        $crate::__macro_handler!{attribute_transparent; #attr=true input: $input, item: $item; $impl; dummy}
[487](https://docs.rs#487)    };
[488](https://docs.rs#488)}
[489](https://docs.rs#489)
[490](https://docs.rs#490)/// Handles [`proc_macro_derive`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/procedural-macros.html#derive-macros)
[491](https://docs.rs#491)/// implementation.
[492](https://docs.rs#492)///
[493](https://docs.rs#493)/// Use [`derive!`] to support [`Parse`] and [`ToTokens`] as well.
[494](https://docs.rs#494)///
[495](https://docs.rs#495)/// Takes any `TokenStream` for `item` and returns any `TokenStream`. `body`
[496](https://docs.rs#496)/// takes a [`DeriveMacroHandler`] with one `TokenStream` parameter. And an
[497](https://docs.rs#497)/// optional [`&mut Emitter`](Emitter) and `&mut TokenStream` for storing a
[498](https://docs.rs#498)/// dummy output.
[499](https://docs.rs#499)///
[500](https://docs.rs#500)/// ```
[501](https://docs.rs#501)/// # use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
[502](https://docs.rs#502)/// # use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
[503](https://docs.rs#503)/// use manyhow::{derive, Emitter, Result};
[504](https://docs.rs#504)/// use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[505](https://docs.rs#505)/// # let item = quote!();
[506](https://docs.rs#506)/// # let output: TokenStream =
[507](https://docs.rs#507)/// derive(
[508](https://docs.rs#508)///     item,
[509](https://docs.rs#509)///     |item: TokenStream, dummy: &mut TokenStream, emitter: &mut Emitter| -> Result {
[510](https://docs.rs#510)///         // ..
[511](https://docs.rs#511)///         # Ok(quote!())
[512](https://docs.rs#512)///     },
[513](https://docs.rs#513)/// );
[514](https://docs.rs#514)/// ```
[515](https://docs.rs#515)pub fn derive<
[516](https://docs.rs#516)    Item: AnyTokenStream,
[517](https://docs.rs#517)    Dummy: AnyTokenStream,
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    Output: MacroOutput,
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    Return: AnyTokenStream,
[520](https://docs.rs#520)    Function,
[521](https://docs.rs#521)>(
[522](https://docs.rs#522)    item: impl AnyTokenStream,
[523](https://docs.rs#523)    body: impl DeriveMacroHandler<Function, Item = Item, Dummy = Dummy, Output = Output>,
[524](https://docs.rs#524)) -> Return {
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    let mut tokens = Dummy::default();
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    let mut emitter = Emitter::new();
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    let output = body.call(item.into().into(), &mut tokens, &mut emitter);
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    let mut tokens = tokens.into();
[529](https://docs.rs#529)    let mut tokens = match output.convert() {
[530](https://docs.rs#530)        Ok(tokens) => tokens,
[531](https://docs.rs#531)        Err(error) => {
[532](https://docs.rs#532)            error.to_tokens(&mut tokens);
[533](https://docs.rs#533)            tokens
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        }
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    };
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    emitter.to_tokens(&mut tokens);
[537](https://docs.rs#537)    tokens.into()
[538](https://docs.rs#538)}
[539](https://docs.rs#539)
[540](https://docs.rs#540)/// Handles [`proc_macro_derive`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/procedural-macros.html#derive-macros)
[541](https://docs.rs#541)/// implementation.
[542](https://docs.rs#542)///
[543](https://docs.rs#543)/// Takes any `TokenStream` for `item` and returns any `TokenStream`. `body`
[544](https://docs.rs#544)/// takes a [`DeriveMacroHandler`] with one `TokenStream` or type implementing
[545](https://docs.rs#545)/// [`Parse`] parameter and returns a `TokenStream` or type implementing
[546](https://docs.rs#546)/// [`ToTokens`]. And an optional [`&mut Emitter`](Emitter) and `&mut
[547](https://docs.rs#547)/// TokenStream` for storing a dummy output.
[548](https://docs.rs#548)///
[549](https://docs.rs#549)/// ```
[550](https://docs.rs#550)/// # use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
[551](https://docs.rs#551)/// # use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
[552](https://docs.rs#552)/// # use syn2 as syn;
[553](https://docs.rs#553)/// use manyhow::{derive, Emitter, Result};
[554](https://docs.rs#554)/// use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[555](https://docs.rs#555)/// # let item = quote!();
[556](https://docs.rs#556)/// # let output: TokenStream =
[557](https://docs.rs#557)/// derive!(item, |item: syn::DeriveInput,
[558](https://docs.rs#558)///                dummy: &mut TokenStream,
[559](https://docs.rs#559)///                emitter: &mut Emitter|
[560](https://docs.rs#560)///  -> Result {
[561](https://docs.rs#561)///     // ..
[562](https://docs.rs#562)///         # Ok(quote!())
[563](https://docs.rs#563)/// });
[564](https://docs.rs#564)/// ```
[565](https://docs.rs#565)#[macro_export]
[566](https://docs.rs#566)macro_rules! derive {
[567](https://docs.rs#567)    ($item:expr, $impl:expr $(,)?) => {
[568](https://docs.rs#568)        $crate::__macro_handler! {derive_transparent; item: $item; $impl}
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    };
[570](https://docs.rs#570)}
[571](https://docs.rs#571)
[572](https://docs.rs#572)/// Handles function like [`proc_macro`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/procedural-macros.html#function-like-procedural-macros)
[573](https://docs.rs#573)/// implementation
[574](https://docs.rs#574)///
[575](https://docs.rs#575)/// Use [`function!`] to support [`Parse`] and [`ToTokens`] as well.
[576](https://docs.rs#576)///
[577](https://docs.rs#577)/// Takes any `TokenStream` for `input` and returns any
[578](https://docs.rs#578)/// `TokenStream`. If `input_as_dummy = true` the item input will be used as
[579](https://docs.rs#579)/// default dummy code on error. `body` takes a [`FunctionMacroHandler`] with
[580](https://docs.rs#580)/// one `TokenStream` parameter. And an optional [`&mut Emitter`](Emitter) and a
[581](https://docs.rs#581)/// `&mut TokenStream` for storing a dummy output.
[582](https://docs.rs#582)///
[583](https://docs.rs#583)/// ```
[584](https://docs.rs#584)/// # use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
[585](https://docs.rs#585)/// # use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
[586](https://docs.rs#586)/// use manyhow::{function, Emitter, Result};
[587](https://docs.rs#587)/// use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[588](https://docs.rs#588)/// # let input = quote!();
[589](https://docs.rs#589)/// # let output: TokenStream =
[590](https://docs.rs#590)/// function(
[591](https://docs.rs#591)///     input,
[592](https://docs.rs#592)///     false,
[593](https://docs.rs#593)///     |input: TokenStream, dummy: &mut TokenStream, emitter: &mut Emitter| -> Result {
[594](https://docs.rs#594)///         // ..
[595](https://docs.rs#595)///         # Ok(quote!())
[596](https://docs.rs#596)///     },
[597](https://docs.rs#597)/// );
[598](https://docs.rs#598)/// ```
[599](https://docs.rs#599)///
[600](https://docs.rs#600)/// *Note:* When `input_as_dummy = true` the `dummy: &mut TokenStream` will be
[601](https://docs.rs#601)/// initialized with `input`. To override assign a new `TokenStream`:
[602](https://docs.rs#602)/// ```
[603](https://docs.rs#603)/// # use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
[604](https://docs.rs#604)/// use manyhow::{function, Result, SilentError};
[605](https://docs.rs#605)/// use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[606](https://docs.rs#606)/// use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
[607](https://docs.rs#607)/// let input = quote!(some input);
[608](https://docs.rs#608)/// let output: TokenStream = function(
[609](https://docs.rs#609)///     input,
[610](https://docs.rs#610)///     true,
[611](https://docs.rs#611)///     |input: TokenStream,
[612](https://docs.rs#612)///      dummy: &mut TokenStream|
[613](https://docs.rs#613)///      -> Result<TokenStream, SilentError> {
[614](https://docs.rs#614)///         assert_tokens!(dummy.to_token_stream(), {
[615](https://docs.rs#615)///             some input
[616](https://docs.rs#616)///         });
[617](https://docs.rs#617)///         *dummy = quote! {
[618](https://docs.rs#618)///             another input
[619](https://docs.rs#619)///         };
[620](https://docs.rs#620)///         // ..
[621](https://docs.rs#621)///         Err(SilentError)
[622](https://docs.rs#622)///     },
[623](https://docs.rs#623)/// );
[624](https://docs.rs#624)///
[625](https://docs.rs#625)/// assert_tokens! {output, {another input}};
[626](https://docs.rs#626)/// ```
[627](https://docs.rs#627)pub fn function<
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    Input: AnyTokenStream,
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    Dummy: AnyTokenStream,
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    Output: MacroOutput,
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    Return: AnyTokenStream,
[632](https://docs.rs#632)    Function,
[633](https://docs.rs#633)>(
[634](https://docs.rs#634)    input: impl AnyTokenStream,
[635](https://docs.rs#635)    input_as_dummy: bool,
[636](https://docs.rs#636)    body: impl FunctionMacroHandler<Function, Input = Input, Dummy = Dummy, Output = Output>,
[637](https://docs.rs#637)) -> Return {
[638](https://docs.rs#638)    let mut tokens = if input_as_dummy {
[639](https://docs.rs#639)        input.clone().into().into()
[640](https://docs.rs#640)    } else {
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        Dummy::default()
[642](https://docs.rs#642)    };
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    let mut emitter = Emitter::new();
[644](https://docs.rs#644)    let output = body.call(input.into().into(), &mut tokens, &mut emitter);
[645](https://docs.rs#645)    let mut tokens = tokens.into();
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    let mut tokens = match output.convert() {
[647](https://docs.rs#647)        Ok(tokens) => tokens,
[648](https://docs.rs#648)        Err(error) => {
[649](https://docs.rs#649)            error.to_tokens(&mut tokens);
[650](https://docs.rs#650)            tokens
[651](https://docs.rs#651)        }
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    };
[653](https://docs.rs#653)    emitter.to_tokens(&mut tokens);
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    tokens.into()
[655](https://docs.rs#655)}
[656](https://docs.rs#656)
[657](https://docs.rs#657)/// Handles function like [`proc_macro`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/procedural-macros.html#function-like-procedural-macros)
[658](https://docs.rs#658)/// implementation
[659](https://docs.rs#659)///
[660](https://docs.rs#660)/// Takes any `TokenStream` for `input` and returns any `TokenStream`. If
[661](https://docs.rs#661)/// `#[as_dummy]` is specified on input, it will be used as default
[662](https://docs.rs#662)/// dummy code on error. `body` takes a [`FunctionMacroHandler`] with one
[663](https://docs.rs#663)/// `TokenStream` or type implementing [`Parse`] parameter and returns a
[664](https://docs.rs#664)/// `TokenStream` or type implementing [`ToTokens`]. And an optional [`&mut
[665](https://docs.rs#665)/// Emitter`](Emitter) and a `&mut TokenStream` for storing a dummy output.
[666](https://docs.rs#666)///
[667](https://docs.rs#667)/// ```
[668](https://docs.rs#668)/// # use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
[669](https://docs.rs#669)/// # use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
[670](https://docs.rs#670)/// # use syn2 as syn;
[671](https://docs.rs#671)/// use manyhow::{function, Emitter, Result};
[672](https://docs.rs#672)/// use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[673](https://docs.rs#673)/// # let input = quote!();
[674](https://docs.rs#674)/// # let output: TokenStream =
[675](https://docs.rs#675)/// function!(input, |input: syn::Item,
[676](https://docs.rs#676)///                   dummy: &mut TokenStream,
[677](https://docs.rs#677)///                   emitter: &mut Emitter|
[678](https://docs.rs#678)///  -> Result<syn::ItemImpl> {
[679](https://docs.rs#679)///     // ..
[680](https://docs.rs#680)///         # manyhow::bail!("unimplemented")
[681](https://docs.rs#681)/// });
[682](https://docs.rs#682)/// ```
[683](https://docs.rs#683)///
[684](https://docs.rs#684)/// *Note:* When `#[as_dummy]` is specified on the input, the `dummy: &mut
[685](https://docs.rs#685)/// TokenStream` will be initialized with `input`. To override assign a new
[686](https://docs.rs#686)/// `TokenStream`:
[687](https://docs.rs#687)///
[688](https://docs.rs#688)/// ```
[689](https://docs.rs#689)/// use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
[690](https://docs.rs#690)/// use manyhow::{function, Result, SilentError};
[691](https://docs.rs#691)/// use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
[692](https://docs.rs#692)/// use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
[693](https://docs.rs#693)///
[694](https://docs.rs#694)/// let input = quote!(some input);
[695](https://docs.rs#695)/// let output: TokenStream = function!(
[696](https://docs.rs#696)///     #[as_dummy] input,
[697](https://docs.rs#697)///     |input: TokenStream, dummy: &mut TokenStream|
[698](https://docs.rs#698)///      -> Result<TokenStream, SilentError> {
[699](https://docs.rs#699)///         assert_tokens!(dummy.to_token_stream(), {
[700](https://docs.rs#700)///             some input
[701](https://docs.rs#701)///         });
[702](https://docs.rs#702)///         *dummy = quote! {
[703](https://docs.rs#703)///             another input
[704](https://docs.rs#704)///         };
[705](https://docs.rs#705)///         // ..
[706](https://docs.rs#706)///         Err(SilentError)
[707](https://docs.rs#707)///     },
[708](https://docs.rs#708)/// );
[709](https://docs.rs#709)///
[710](https://docs.rs#710)/// assert_tokens! {output, {another input}};
[711](https://docs.rs#711)/// ```
[712](https://docs.rs#712)#[macro_export]
[713](https://docs.rs#713)macro_rules! function {
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    (#[as_dummy] $input:expr, $impl:expr $(,)?) => {
[715](https://docs.rs#715)        $crate::__macro_handler! {function_transparent; input: $input; $impl; dummy: $input}
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    };

[757](https://docs.rs#757)macro_rules! macro_input {
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    ($MacroInput:ident; $($input:ident: $Input:ident),+; $a:literal; $name:literal; $token_streams:literal) => {
[759](https://docs.rs#759)        /// Input of
[760](https://docs.rs#760)        #[doc = $a]
[761](https://docs.rs#761)        #[doc = $name]
[762](https://docs.rs#762)        /// proc-macro
[763](https://docs.rs#763)        ///
[764](https://docs.rs#764)        /// Note: for `TokenStream` either [`proc_macro::TokenStream`] or
[765](https://docs.rs#765)        /// [`proc_macro2::TokenStream`] can be used.
[766](https://docs.rs#766)        ///
[767](https://docs.rs#767)        /// Trait is implemented for any [`function`](FnOnce), taking in
[768](https://docs.rs#768)        #[doc = concat!($token_streams, ".")]
[769](https://docs.rs#769)        /// Additionally, they can take optionally in any order a [`&mut
[770](https://docs.rs#770)        /// Emitter`](Emitter) which allows emitting errors without returning early. And
[771](https://docs.rs#771)        /// a `&mut TokenStream` to return a dummy `TokenStream` on failure.
[772](https://docs.rs#772)        ///
[773](https://docs.rs#773)        /// When used with
[774](https://docs.rs#774)        #[doc = concat!("[`", $name, "()`]")]
[775](https://docs.rs#775)        /// it must return a type implementing [`MacroOutput`], with
[776](https://docs.rs#776)        #[doc = concat!("[`", $name, "!`]")]
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        /// it can accept types implementing [`Parse`] and return types
[778](https://docs.rs#778)        /// implementing [`ToTokens`](quote::ToTokens).
[779](https://docs.rs#779)        #[allow(missing_docs)]
[780](https://docs.rs#780)        pub trait $MacroInput<Function> {
[781](https://docs.rs#781)            $(type $Input;)+
[782](https://docs.rs#782)            type Dummy;
[783](https://docs.rs#783)            type Output;
[784](https://docs.rs#784)            #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
[785](https://docs.rs#785)            fn call(
[786](https://docs.rs#786)                self,
[787](https://docs.rs#787)                $(item: Self::$Input,)+
[788](https://docs.rs#788)                dummy: &mut Self::Dummy,
[789](https://docs.rs#789)                emitter: &mut Emitter,
[790](https://docs.rs#790)            ) -> Self::Output;
[791](https://docs.rs#791)        }
[792](https://docs.rs#792)
[793](https://docs.rs#793)        macro_input_impl!([$($Input,)+ Dummy: Clone]; $MacroInput; $($input: $Input),*; &mut Dummy, &mut Emitter; dummy: Dummy dummy; emitter emitter);
[794](https://docs.rs#794)        macro_input_impl!([$($Input,)+ Dummy: Clone]; $MacroInput; $($input: $Input),*; &mut Dummy; dummy: Dummy dummy; _emitter);
[795](https://docs.rs#795)        macro_input_impl!([$($Input),+]; $MacroInput; $($input: $Input),*; &mut Emitter; _dummy: TokenStream; emitter emitter);
[796](https://docs.rs#796)        macro_input_impl!([$($Input),+]; $MacroInput; $($input: $Input),*; ; _dummy: TokenStream; _emitter);
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    };
[798](https://docs.rs#798)}
[799](https://docs.rs#799)
[800](https://docs.rs#800)macro_rules! macro_input_impl {

[802](https://docs.rs#802)        impl<$($gen)*, Output, Function> $MacroInput<($($Input,)+ $($Extra,)* Output)> for Function

[818](https://docs.rs#818)        }

[820](https://docs.rs#820)    }

[829](https://docs.rs#829)/// Output of a macro handler.

[831](https://docs.rs#831)/// Enables support for returning any [`TokenStream`](AnyTokenStream) or

# ToTokensError in manyhow - Rust

# function in manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/0.11.4/manyhow/fn.function.html

`pub fn function<Input: `[AnyTokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html), Dummy: [AnyTokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html), Output: [MacroOutput](https://docs.rs/trait.MacroOutput.html), Return: [AnyTokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html), Function>(
    input: impl [AnyTokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html),
    input_as_dummy: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    body: impl [FunctionMacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.FunctionMacroHandler.html)<Function, Input = Input, Dummy = Dummy, Output = Output>,
) -> Return## Expand description

Handles function like [ proc_macro](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/procedural-macros.html#function-like-procedural-macros)
implementation

Use [ function!](https://docs.rs/macro.function.html) to support

[and](https://docs.rs/syn/1.0.109/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/syn/parse/trait.Parse.html)

`Parse`[as well.](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/quote/to_tokens/trait.ToTokens.html)

`ToTokens`Takes any `TokenStream` for `input` and returns any
`TokenStream`. If `input_as_dummy = true` the item input will be used as
default dummy code on error. `body` takes a [ FunctionMacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.FunctionMacroHandler.html) with
one

`TokenStream` parameter. And an optional [and a](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

`&mut Emitter``&mut TokenStream` for storing a dummy output.```
use manyhow::{function, Emitter, Result};
use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
function(
    input,
    false,
    |input: TokenStream, dummy: &mut TokenStream, emitter: &mut Emitter| -> Result {
        // ..
    },
);
```
*Note:* When `input_as_dummy = true` the `dummy: &mut TokenStream` will be
initialized with `input`. To override assign a new `TokenStream`:

```
use manyhow::{function, Result, SilentError};
use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
let input = quote!(some input);
let output: TokenStream = function(
    input,
    true,
    |input: TokenStream,
     dummy: &mut TokenStream|
     -> Result<TokenStream, SilentError> {
        assert_tokens!(dummy.to_token_stream(), {
            some input
        });
        *dummy = quote! {
            another input
        };
        // ..
        Err(SilentError)
    },
);
assert_tokens! {output, {another input}};
```

# function in manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/0.11.4/manyhow/macro.function.html

```
macro_rules! function {
    (#[as_dummy] $input:expr, $impl:expr $(,)?) => { ... };
    ($input:expr, $impl:expr $(,)?) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Handles function like [ proc_macro](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/procedural-macros.html#function-like-procedural-macros)
implementation

Takes any `TokenStream` for `input` and returns any `TokenStream`. If
`#[as_dummy]` is specified on input, it will be used as default
dummy code on error. `body` takes a [ FunctionMacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.FunctionMacroHandler.html) with one

`TokenStream` or type implementing [parameter and returns a](https://docs.rs/syn/1.0.109/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/syn/parse/trait.Parse.html)

`Parse``TokenStream` or type implementing [. And an optional](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/quote/to_tokens/trait.ToTokens.html)

`ToTokens`[and a](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

`&mut Emitter``&mut TokenStream` for storing a dummy output.```
use manyhow::{function, Emitter, Result};
use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
function!(input, |input: syn::Item,
                  dummy: &mut TokenStream,
                  emitter: &mut Emitter|
 -> Result<syn::ItemImpl> {
    // ..
});
```
*Note:* When `#[as_dummy]` is specified on the input, the `dummy: &mut TokenStream` will be initialized with `input`. To override assign a new
`TokenStream`:

```
use proc_macro_utils::assert_tokens;
use manyhow::{function, Result, SilentError};
use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
let input = quote!(some input);
let output: TokenStream = function!(
    #[as_dummy] input,
    |input: TokenStream, dummy: &mut TokenStream|
     -> Result<TokenStream, SilentError> {
        assert_tokens!(dummy.to_token_stream(), {
            some input
        });
        *dummy = quote! {
            another input
        };
        // ..
        Err(SilentError)
    },
);
assert_tokens! {output, {another input}};
```

# attribute in manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/0.11.4/manyhow/fn.attribute.html

`pub fn attribute<Input: `[AnyTokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html), Item: [AnyTokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html), Dummy: [AnyTokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html), Output: [MacroOutput](https://docs.rs/trait.MacroOutput.html), Return: [AnyTokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html), Function>(
    input: impl [AnyTokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html),
    item: impl [AnyTokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html),
    item_as_dummy: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    body: impl [AttributeMacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.AttributeMacroHandler.html)<Function, Item = Item, Input = Input, Dummy = Dummy, Output = Output>,
) -> Return## Expand description

Handles [ proc_macro_attribute](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/procedural-macros.html#attribute-macros)
implementation

Takes any `TokenStream` for `input` and `item` and returns any
`TokenStream`. If `item_as_dummy = true` the item input will be used as
default dummy code on error. `body` takes a [ AttributeMacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.AttributeMacroHandler.html) with
two

`TokenStream` parameters. And an optional [and a](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

`&mut Emitter``&mut TokenStream` for storing a dummy output.```
use manyhow::{attribute, Emitter, Result};
use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
attribute(
    input,
    item,
    false,
    |input: TokenStream,
     item: TokenStream,
     dummy: &mut TokenStream,
     emitter: &mut Emitter|
     -> Result {
        // ..
    },
);
```
*Note:* When `item_as_dummy = true` the `dummy: &mut TokenStream` will be
initialized with `item`. To override assign a new `TokenStream`:

```
use manyhow::{attribute, Result, SilentError};
use proc_macro2::TokenStream;
use quote::{quote, ToTokens};
let item = quote!(
    struct Struct;
);
let output: TokenStream = attribute(
    input,
    item,
    true,
    |input: TokenStream,
     item: TokenStream,
     dummy: &mut TokenStream|
     -> Result<TokenStream, SilentError> {
        assert_tokens!(dummy.to_token_stream(), {
            struct Struct;
        });
        *dummy = quote! {
            struct Struct(HelloWorld);
        };
        // ..
        Err(SilentError)
    },
);
assert_tokens! {output, {struct Struct(HelloWorld);}};
```

# attribute in manyhow - Rust

`TokenStream`s or types implementing [parameters and returning a](https://docs.rs/syn/1.0.109/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/syn/parse/trait.Parse.html)

);

    input,

# bail in manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/0.11.4/manyhow/macro.bail.html

# Macro bail

[Source](../src/manyhow/macro_rules.rs.html#128-138) ```
macro_rules! bail {
    ($msg:literal) => { ... };
    ($error:expr) => { ... };
    ($($tt:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```

## Expand description

Exit by returning error, matching `anyhow::bail!`

The syntax is identical to `error_message!`

[ⓘ](#)```
bail!("an error message"; error = "with attachments");
let span = Span::call_site();
bail!(span, "error message");
let error = syn::Error::new(Span::call_site(), "an error");
bail!(error);
```

---

# emit in manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/0.11.4/manyhow/macro.emit.html

```
macro_rules! emit {
    ($emitter:expr, $msg:literal) => { ... };
    ($emitter:expr, $error:expr) => { ... };
    ($emitter:expr, $($tt:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Push an error to an emitter.

The syntax is identical to [ error_message!](https://docs.rs/macro.error_message.html) and

[, but the first argument is the](https://docs.rs/macro.bail.html)

`bail!`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

`Emitter````
let mut emitter = Emitter::new();
emit!(emitter, "an error message");
emit!(emitter, "an error message"; error = "with attachments");
let span = Span::call_site();
emit!(emitter, span, "error message");
let error = syn::Error::new(Span::call_site(), "an error");
emit!(emitter, error);
```
It can also be used with [ Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html).

```
let mut error: Error = error_message!("initial error").into();
emit!(error, "an error message");
```
Or any collection implementing [ Extend](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.Extend.html).

```
let mut errors = Vec::new();
emit!(errors, "an error message");
```

---

# ensure in manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/0.11.4/manyhow/macro.ensure.html

```
macro_rules! ensure {
    ($cond:expr, $($bail_args:tt)*) => { ... };
    (let $pat:pat = $expr:expr, $($bail_args:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Return early with an error, if a condition is not satisfied, matching
[ anyhow::ensure!](https://docs.rs/anyhow/latest/anyhow/macro.ensure.html).

The syntax is identical to [ bail!](https://docs.rs/macro.bail.html), with an additional leading condition.

Additional to a boolean expression, the expression can also be a `let ... = ...` pattern matching, and will expand to `let ... else`.

```
ensure!(true, "an error message"; help = "with attachments");
ensure!(let Some(a) = Some(1), "error");
assert_eq!(a, 1);
```

---

# error_message in manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/0.11.4/manyhow/macro.error_message.html

```
macro_rules! error_message {
    ($fmt:literal $($tt:tt)*) => { ... };
    ($span:expr, $fmt:literal $($tt:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Creates an [ ErrorMessage](https://docs.rs/struct.ErrorMessage.html), comparable to the

[macro](https://docs.rs/anyhow/latest/anyhow/macro.anyhow.html)

`anyhow!`If the first argument is not a literal it is taken as the span of the error.
The span expression can **either** implement [ SpanRanged](https://docs.rs/trait.SpanRanged.html) or implement

[. Otherwise,](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/quote/to_tokens/trait.ToTokens.html)

`ToTokens`[is used.](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/struct.Span.html#method.call_site)

`Span::call_site````
assert_eq!(
    error_message!("format {} string{named}", "<3", named = "!").to_string(),
    "format <3 string!"
);
// Span can either be `proc_macro::Span` or `proc_macro2::Span`
assert_eq!(
    error_message!(Span::call_site(), "spanned error").to_string(),
    "spanned error"
);
// Or any expression implementing `quote::ToTokens`
assert_eq!(
    error_message!(quote!(some tokens), "spanned error").to_string(),
    "spanned error"
);
```
On top of the standard [ format_args!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.format_args.html) parameters additional attachments
can be specified delimited with

`;`.```
assert_eq!(
    error_message!(
        "format {} string{named}", "<3", named = "!";
        error = "some additional error";
        info = "some info as well";
        custom_attachment = "amazing"
    ).to_string(),
    "format <3 string!
  = error: some additional error
  = info: some info as well
  = custom_attachment: amazing
"
);
```

---

# SpanRanged in manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/0.11.4/manyhow/trait.SpanRanged.html

```
pub trait SpanRanged {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[span_range](https://docs.rs#tymethod.span_range)(&self) -> [Range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.Range.html)<[Span](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/struct.Span.html)> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs);
    // Provided method
    fn [span_joined](https://docs.rs#method.span_joined)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Span](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/struct.Span.html)> { ... }
}## Expand description

Returns the `Range`[ <Span>](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/struct.Span.html) from the start to the end of
multi-token structures.

`start` and `end` can be the same when called on single Tokens or [ Span](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/struct.Span.html).

Due to compiler limitations, it is currently not possible to implement
`SpanRanged for T: ToTokens`, therefor there is
[ to_tokens_span_range()](https://docs.rs/fn.to_tokens_span_range.html).

For types that **either** implement [ SpanRanged](https://docs.rs/trait.SpanRanged.html) or

[(but](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/quote/to_tokens/trait.ToTokens.html)

`ToTokens`**NOT**both) the

[macro can be used as well.](https://docs.rs/macro.span_range.html)

`span_range!`[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

This is superior to a normal [ Span](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/struct.Span.html) (at least until

[works on stable), because it leads to better error messages:](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/struct.Span.html#method.join)

`Span::join`Given the following expression

`let a = |something: usize| something;`[ ErrorMessage::new(first_pipe_span, "error message")](https://docs.rs/struct.ErrorMessage.html#method.new)
would result in something like

```
error: error message
let a = |something: usize| something;
        ^
```
While [ ErrorMessage::new(first_pipe_span..something_span, "error message")](https://docs.rs/struct.ErrorMessage.html#method.new) would improve the error message to:

```
error: error message
let a = |something: usize| something;
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

# JoinToTokensError in manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/0.11.4/manyhow/trait.JoinToTokensError.html

```
pub trait JoinToTokensError {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[join](https://docs.rs#tymethod.join)(self, error: impl [ToTokensError](https://docs.rs/trait.ToTokensError.html) + 'static) -> [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html);
}## Expand description

Allows to call `.join(..)` on any `impl ToTokensError`

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/manyhow/error.rs.html#372)#### fn [join](https://docs.rs#tymethod.join)(self, error: impl [ToTokensError](https://docs.rs/trait.ToTokensError.html) + 'static) -> [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/manyhow/error.rs.html#372)

#### fn [join](https://docs.rs#tymethod.join)(self, error: impl [ToTokensError](https://docs.rs/trait.ToTokensError.html) + 'static) -> [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)

Joins two `Error`s

```
use manyhow::error_message;
error_message!("test").join(error_message!("another"));
```
Some errors like [`manyhow::Error`] and [`manyhow::ErrorMessage`] can
also be “added”:

```
use manyhow::{error_message, Error};
error_message!("Hello Rust!") + error_message!("Hello 🦀!")
Error::from(error_message!("Hello Rust!")) + error_message!("Hello 🦀!")
```
## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

# manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/manyhow/

## Expand description

Proc **m**acro **anyhow**, a combination of ideas from
[ anyhow](https://docs.rs/docs.rs/anyhow) and

[to improve proc macro development, especially focused on the error handling.](https://docs.rs/docs.rs/proc-macro-error)

`proc-macro-error`[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

Error handling in proc-macros is unideal, as the top level functions of
proc-macros can only return `TokenStreams` both in success and failure case.
This means that I often write code like this, moving the actual
implementation in a separate function to be able to use the ergonomic rust
error handling with e.g., `?`.

```
use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
#[proc_macro]
pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    match actual_implementation(input.into()) {
        Ok(output) => output,
        Err(error) => error.into_compile_error(),
    }
    .into()
}
fn actual_implementation(input: TokenStream2) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
    // ..
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#using-the-manyhow-macro)Using the `#[manyhow]` macro

To activate the error handling, just add [ #[manyhow]](https://docs.rs/attr.manyhow.html) above any
proc-macro implementation, reducing the above example to:

```
use manyhow::manyhow;
use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
#[manyhow]
#[proc_macro]
// You can also merge the two attributes: #[manyhow(proc_macro)]
fn my_macro(input: TokenStream2) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
    // ..
}
// On top of the TokenStreams any type that implements [`Parse`] is supported
#[manyhow(proc_macro_derive(MyMacro))]
#[proc_macro]
// The output can also be anything that implements `quote::ToTokens`
fn my_derive_macro(input: syn::DeriveInput) -> manyhow::Result<syn::ItemImpl> {
    // ..
}
```
See [Without macros](https://docs.rs#without-macros) to see what this expands to under the
hood.

You can also use the `#[manyhow]` attributes on a use statement, useful when
moving your proc-macro implementations in separate modules.

```
use manyhow::manyhow;
mod module {
    use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
    pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream2) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
        // ..
    }
}
#[manyhow]
#[proc_macro]
// You can also merge the two attributes: #[manyhow(proc_macro)]
pub use module::my_macro;
```
A proc macro function marked as `#[manyhow]` can take and return any
[ TokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html), and can also return

`Result<TokenStream, E>` where `E` implements [. As additional parameters a](https://docs.rs/trait.ToTokensError.html)

`ToTokensError`[dummy](https://docs.rs#dummy-mut-tokenstream)and/or

[emitter](https://docs.rs#emitter-mut-emitter)can be specified.

The `manyhow` attribute takes optional flags to configure its behavior.

When used for `proc_macro` and `proc_macro_attribute`,
`#[manyhow(input_as_dummy, ...)]` will take the input of a function like
`proc_macro` to initialize the [dummy `&mut TokenStream`](#
dummy-mut-tokenstream) while `#[manyhow(item_as_dummy, ...)]` on
`proc_macro_attribute` will initialize the dummy with the annotated item.

You can merge the `#[proc_macro*]` attribute inside the manyhow flags e.g.,
`#[manyhow(proc_macro)]` or `#[manyhow(proc_macro_derive(SomeTrait, ...))]`.

The `#[manyhow(impl_fn, ...)]` flag will put the actual macro implementation
in a separate function. Making it available for e.g., unit testing with
[ proc_macro_utils::assert_expansion!](https://docs.rs/proc-macro-utils/latest/proc_macro_utils/macro.assert_expansion.html).

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[manyhow(impl_fn)]
#[proc_macro]
pub fn actual_macro(input: TokenStream2) -> TokenStream2 {
    // ...
}
// would roughly expand to
#[proc_macro]
pub fn actual_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    actual_macro_impl(input.into()).into()
}
fn actual_macro_impl(input: TokenStream2) -> TokenStream2 {
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#without-macros)Without macros

`manyhow` can be used without proc macros, and they can be disabled by
adding `manyhow` with `default-features=false`.

The usage is more or less the same, though with some added boilerplate from
needing to invoke one of [ function()](https://docs.rs/fn.function.html) (

[),](https://docs.rs/macro.function.html)

`function!`[(](https://docs.rs/fn.attribute.html)

`attribute()`[) or](https://docs.rs/macro.attribute.html)

`attribute!`[(](https://docs.rs/fn.derive.html)

`derive()`[) directly. For each version there exists a function and a](https://docs.rs/macro.derive.html)

`derive!``macro_rules` macro, while the function only
supports [and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html)

`proc_macro::TokenStream`[, the macro versions also support any type that implements](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/i686-pc-windows-msvc/proc_macro2/struct.TokenStream.html)

`proc_macro2::TokenStream`[and](https://docs.rs/syn/1.0.109/i686-pc-windows-msvc/syn/parse/trait.Parse.html)

`Parse`[respectively.](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/i686-pc-windows-msvc/quote/to_tokens/trait.ToTokens.html)

`ToTokens`While the examples use closures, functions can be passed in as well. The above example would then change to:

```
use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
#[proc_macro]
pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    manyhow::function(
        input,
        false,
        |input: TokenStream2| -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
            // ..
        },
    )
    // Or
    manyhow::function!(
        input,
        |input: syn::DeriveInput| -> manyhow::Result<syn::ItemImpl> {
            // ..
        },
    )
}
```
[ Emitter](https://docs.rs#emitter-mut-emitter) and

[dummy](https://docs.rs#dummy-mut-tokenstream)can also be used.

`TokenStream`[(](https://docs.rs/fn.function.html)

`function()`[) and](https://docs.rs/macro.function.html)

`function!`[(](https://docs.rs/fn.attribute.html)

`attribute()`[) take an additional boolean parameter controlling whether the input/item will be used as initial dummy.](https://docs.rs/macro.attribute.html)

`attribute!`[§](https://docs.rs#emitter-mut-emitter)`emitter: &mut Emitter`

[ *MacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.FunctionMacroHandler.html)s (the traits defining what
closures/functions can be used with

`manyhow`) can take a mutable reference
to an [. This allows collecting errors, but not fail immediately.](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

`Emitter`[ Emitter::into_result](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html#method.into_result) can be used to return if an

[contains any values.](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

`Emitter````
use manyhow::{manyhow, Emitter, ErrorMessage};
use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
#[manyhow]
#[proc_macro]
fn my_macro(input: TokenStream2, emitter: &mut Emitter) -> manyhow::Result<TokenStream2> {
    // ..
    emitter.emit(ErrorMessage::call_site("A fun error!"));
    emitter.into_result()?;
    // ..
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#dummy-mut-tokenstream)`dummy: &mut TokenStream`

[ *MacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.FunctionMacroHandler.html)s can also take a mutable reference
to a

`TokenStream`, to enable emitting some dummy code to be used in case
the macro errors.This allows either appending tokens e.g., with [ ToTokens::to_tokens](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/i686-pc-windows-msvc/quote/to_tokens/trait.ToTokens.html#tymethod.to_tokens) or
directly setting the dummy code e.g.,

`*dummy = quote!{some tokens}`.[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

- `macros`- **default**Enables- `#[manyhow]`
- `syn`/- `syn2`- **default**Enables errors for- `syn`2.x
- `syn1`Enables errors for- `syn`1.x
- `darling`Enables errors for- `darling`

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [attribute](https://docs.rs/macro.attribute.html)
- Handles `proc_macro_attribute`
- [bail](https://docs.rs/macro.bail.html)
- Exit by returning error, matching `anyhow::bail!`
- [derive](https://docs.rs/macro.derive.html)
- Handles `proc_macro_derive`
- [emit](https://docs.rs/macro.emit.html)
- Push an error to an emitter.
- [ensure](https://docs.rs/macro.ensure.html)
- Return early with an error, if a condition is not satisfied, matching
`anyhow::ensure!`
- [error_](https://docs.rs/macro.error_message.html)- message
- Creates an `ErrorMessage``anyhow!`
- [function](https://docs.rs/macro.function.html)
- Handles function like `proc_macro`
- [span_](https://docs.rs/macro.span_range.html)- range
- Get a `Range``<Span>`**either**implements`SpanRanged``ToTokens`**NOT**both).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Emitter](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)
- Allows emitting errors without returning.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- This crates Error type
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.ErrorMessage.html)- Message
- A single error message
- [Silent](https://docs.rs/struct.SilentError.html)- Error
- Error that does not expand to any `compile_error!`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [AnyToken](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html)- Stream
- Marker trait for `proc_macro::TokenStream``proc_macro2::TokenStream`
- [Attachment](https://docs.rs/trait.Attachment.html)
- Exposes `ErrorMessage::attachment``ResultExt::attachment`
- [Attribute](https://docs.rs/trait.AttributeMacroHandler.html)- Macro - Handler
- Input of an attribute proc-macro
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/trait.DeriveMacroHandler.html)- Macro - Handler
- Input of a derive proc-macro
- [Function](https://docs.rs/trait.FunctionMacroHandler.html)- Macro - Handler
- Input of a function proc-macro
- [Join](https://docs.rs/trait.JoinToTokensError.html)- ToTokens - Error
- Allows to call `.join(..)`on any`impl ToTokensError`
- [Macro](https://docs.rs/trait.MacroOutput.html)- Output
- Output of a macro handler.
- [Result](https://docs.rs/trait.ResultExt.html)- Ext
- Some utilities on `Result<T, impl ToTokensError>`
- [Span](https://docs.rs/trait.SpanRanged.html)- Ranged
- Returns the `Range``<Span>`
- [ToTokens](https://docs.rs/trait.ToTokensError.html)- Error
- Error that can be converted to a `TokenStream``MacroOutput`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [attribute](https://docs.rs/fn.attribute.html)
- Handles `proc_macro_attribute`
- [derive](https://docs.rs/fn.derive.html)
- Handles `proc_macro_derive`
- [function](https://docs.rs/fn.function.html)
- Handles function like `proc_macro`
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_tokens_span_range.html)- tokens_ - span_ - range
- Implementation of `SpanRanged``for T:``ToTokens`

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [manyhow](https://docs.rs/attr.manyhow.html)- `macros`
- Attribute macro to remove boilerplate from proc macro entry points.

[dummy](https://docs.rs#dummy-mut-tokenstream)can also be used.

`TokenStream`[(](https://docs.rs/fn.function.html)

`function()`[) and](https://docs.rs/macro.function.html)

`function!`[(](https://docs.rs/fn.attribute.html)

`attribute()`[) take an additional boolean parameter controlling whether the input/item will be used as initial dummy.](https://docs.rs/macro.attribute.html)

`attribute!`[§](https://docs.rs#emitter-mut-emitter)`emitter: &mut Emitter`

[ *MacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.FunctionMacroHandler.html)s (the traits defining what
closures/functions can be used with

`manyhow`) can take a mutable reference
to an [. This allows collecting errors, but not fail immediately.](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

`Emitter`[ Emitter::into_result](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html#method.into_result) can be used to return if an

[contains any values.](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

`Emitter````
use manyhow::{manyhow, Emitter, ErrorMessage};
use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
#[manyhow]
#[proc_macro]
fn my_macro(input: TokenStream2, emitter: &mut Emitter) -> manyhow::Result<TokenStream2> {
    // ..
    emitter.emit(ErrorMessage::call_site("A fun error!"));
    emitter.into_result()?;
    // ..
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#dummy-mut-tokenstream)`dummy: &mut TokenStream`

[ *MacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.FunctionMacroHandler.html)s can also take a mutable reference
to a

`TokenStream`, to enable emitting some dummy code to be used in case
the macro errors.This allows either appending tokens e.g., with [ ToTokens::to_tokens](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/quote/to_tokens/trait.ToTokens.html#tymethod.to_tokens) or
directly setting the dummy code e.g.,

`*dummy = quote!{some tokens}`.[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

- `macros`- **default**Enables- `#[manyhow]`
- `syn`/- `syn2`- **default**Enables errors for- `syn`2.x
- `syn1`Enables errors for- `syn`1.x
- `darling`Enables errors for- `darling`

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [attribute](https://docs.rs/macro.attribute.html)
- Handles `proc_macro_attribute`
- [bail](https://docs.rs/macro.bail.html)
- Exit by returning error, matching `anyhow::bail!`
- [derive](https://docs.rs/macro.derive.html)
- Handles `proc_macro_derive`
- [emit](https://docs.rs/macro.emit.html)
- Push an error to an emitter.
- [ensure](https://docs.rs/macro.ensure.html)
- Return early with an error, if a condition is not satisfied, matching
`anyhow::ensure!`
- [error_](https://docs.rs/macro.error_message.html)- message
- Creates an `ErrorMessage``anyhow!`
- [function](https://docs.rs/macro.function.html)
- Handles function like `proc_macro`
- [span_](https://docs.rs/macro.span_range.html)- range
- Get a `Range``<Span>`**either**implements`SpanRanged``ToTokens`**NOT**both).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Emitter](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)
- Allows emitting errors without returning.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- This crates Error type
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.ErrorMessage.html)- Message
- A single error message
- [Silent](https://docs.rs/struct.SilentError.html)- Error
- Error that does not expand to any `compile_error!`

- Input of a function proc-macro

- Allows to call `.join(..)`on any`impl ToTokensError`

- Output of a macro handler.

# manyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/manyhow/latest/x86_64-apple-darwin/manyhow/

## Expand description

Proc **m**acro **anyhow**, a combination of ideas from
[ anyhow](https://docs.rs/docs.rs/anyhow) and

[to improve proc macro development, especially focused on the error handling.](https://docs.rs/docs.rs/proc-macro-error)

`proc-macro-error`[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

Error handling in proc-macros is unideal, as the top level functions of
proc-macros can only return `TokenStreams` both in success and failure case.
This means that I often write code like this, moving the actual
implementation in a separate function to be able to use the ergonomic rust
error handling with e.g., `?`.

```
use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
#[proc_macro]
pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    match actual_implementation(input.into()) {
        Ok(output) => output,
        Err(error) => error.into_compile_error(),
    }
    .into()
}
fn actual_implementation(input: TokenStream2) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
    // ..
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#using-the-manyhow-macro)Using the `#[manyhow]` macro

To activate the error handling, just add [ #[manyhow]](https://docs.rs/attr.manyhow.html) above any
proc-macro implementation, reducing the above example to:

```
use manyhow::manyhow;
use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
#[manyhow]
#[proc_macro]
// You can also merge the two attributes: #[manyhow(proc_macro)]
fn my_macro(input: TokenStream2) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
    // ..
}
// On top of the TokenStreams any type that implements [`Parse`] is supported
#[manyhow(proc_macro_derive(MyMacro))]
#[proc_macro]
// The output can also be anything that implements `quote::ToTokens`
fn my_derive_macro(input: syn::DeriveInput) -> manyhow::Result<syn::ItemImpl> {
    // ..
}
```
See [Without macros](https://docs.rs#without-macros) to see what this expands to under the
hood.

You can also use the `#[manyhow]` attributes on a use statement, useful when
moving your proc-macro implementations in separate modules.

```
use manyhow::manyhow;
mod module {
    use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
    pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream2) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
        // ..
    }
}
#[manyhow]
#[proc_macro]
// You can also merge the two attributes: #[manyhow(proc_macro)]
pub use module::my_macro;
```
A proc macro function marked as `#[manyhow]` can take and return any
[ TokenStream](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyTokenStream.html), and can also return

`Result<TokenStream, E>` where `E` implements [. As additional parameters a](https://docs.rs/trait.ToTokensError.html)

`ToTokensError`[dummy](https://docs.rs#dummy-mut-tokenstream)and/or

[emitter](https://docs.rs#emitter-mut-emitter)can be specified.

The `manyhow` attribute takes optional flags to configure its behavior.

When used for `proc_macro` and `proc_macro_attribute`,
`#[manyhow(input_as_dummy, ...)]` will take the input of a function like
`proc_macro` to initialize the [dummy `&mut TokenStream`](#
dummy-mut-tokenstream) while `#[manyhow(item_as_dummy, ...)]` on
`proc_macro_attribute` will initialize the dummy with the annotated item.

You can merge the `#[proc_macro*]` attribute inside the manyhow flags e.g.,
`#[manyhow(proc_macro)]` or `#[manyhow(proc_macro_derive(SomeTrait, ...))]`.

The `#[manyhow(impl_fn, ...)]` flag will put the actual macro implementation
in a separate function. Making it available for e.g., unit testing with
[ proc_macro_utils::assert_expansion!](https://docs.rs/proc-macro-utils/latest/proc_macro_utils/macro.assert_expansion.html).

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[manyhow(impl_fn)]
#[proc_macro]
pub fn actual_macro(input: TokenStream2) -> TokenStream2 {
    // ...
}
// would roughly expand to
#[proc_macro]
pub fn actual_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    actual_macro_impl(input.into()).into()
}
fn actual_macro_impl(input: TokenStream2) -> TokenStream2 {
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#without-macros)Without macros

`manyhow` can be used without proc macros, and they can be disabled by
adding `manyhow` with `default-features=false`.

The usage is more or less the same, though with some added boilerplate from
needing to invoke one of [ function()](https://docs.rs/fn.function.html) (

[),](https://docs.rs/macro.function.html)

`function!`[(](https://docs.rs/fn.attribute.html)

`attribute()`[) or](https://docs.rs/macro.attribute.html)

`attribute!`[(](https://docs.rs/fn.derive.html)

`derive()`[) directly. For each version there exists a function and a](https://docs.rs/macro.derive.html)

`derive!``macro_rules` macro, while the function only
supports [and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html)

`proc_macro::TokenStream`[, the macro versions also support any type that implements](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.95/x86_64-apple-darwin/proc_macro2/struct.TokenStream.html)

`proc_macro2::TokenStream`[and](https://docs.rs/syn/1.0.109/x86_64-apple-darwin/syn/parse/trait.Parse.html)

`Parse`[respectively.](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/x86_64-apple-darwin/quote/to_tokens/trait.ToTokens.html)

`ToTokens`While the examples use closures, functions can be passed in as well. The above example would then change to:

```
use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
#[proc_macro]
pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    manyhow::function(
        input,
        false,
        |input: TokenStream2| -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
            // ..
        },
    )
    // Or
    manyhow::function!(
        input,
        |input: syn::DeriveInput| -> manyhow::Result<syn::ItemImpl> {
            // ..
        },
    )
}
```
[ Emitter](https://docs.rs#emitter-mut-emitter) and

[dummy](https://docs.rs#dummy-mut-tokenstream)can also be used.

`TokenStream`[(](https://docs.rs/fn.function.html)

`function()`[) and](https://docs.rs/macro.function.html)

`function!`[(](https://docs.rs/fn.attribute.html)

`attribute()`[) take an additional boolean parameter controlling whether the input/item will be used as initial dummy.](https://docs.rs/macro.attribute.html)

`attribute!`[§](https://docs.rs#emitter-mut-emitter)`emitter: &mut Emitter`

[ *MacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.FunctionMacroHandler.html)s (the traits defining what
closures/functions can be used with

`manyhow`) can take a mutable reference
to an [. This allows collecting errors, but not fail immediately.](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

`Emitter`[ Emitter::into_result](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html#method.into_result) can be used to return if an

[contains any values.](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

`Emitter````
use manyhow::{manyhow, Emitter, ErrorMessage};
use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
#[manyhow]
#[proc_macro]
fn my_macro(input: TokenStream2, emitter: &mut Emitter) -> manyhow::Result<TokenStream2> {
    // ..
    emitter.emit(ErrorMessage::call_site("A fun error!"));
    emitter.into_result()?;
    // ..
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#dummy-mut-tokenstream)`dummy: &mut TokenStream`

[ *MacroHandler](https://docs.rs/trait.FunctionMacroHandler.html)s can also take a mutable reference
to a

`TokenStream`, to enable emitting some dummy code to be used in case
the macro errors.This allows either appending tokens e.g., with [ ToTokens::to_tokens](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.40/x86_64-apple-darwin/quote/to_tokens/trait.ToTokens.html#tymethod.to_tokens) or
directly setting the dummy code e.g.,

`*dummy = quote!{some tokens}`.[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

- `macros`- **default**Enables- `#[manyhow]`
- `syn`/- `syn2`- **default**Enables errors for- `syn`2.x
- `syn1`Enables errors for- `syn`1.x
- `darling`Enables errors for- `darling`

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [attribute](https://docs.rs/macro.attribute.html)
- Handles `proc_macro_attribute`
- [bail](https://docs.rs/macro.bail.html)
- Exit by returning error, matching `anyhow::bail!`
- [derive](https://docs.rs/macro.derive.html)
